clue.text: Money we brought back for nut

parts.note: cash is money in hand

indicators.note: brought back means the word we is read from its end to its start

explanation.surface: Someone pays cash and walks away with a bag of nuts.
explanation.definitionFit: The kidney-shaped cashew is an edible nut from a tropical tree.

clue.text: See eye to eye in Gretna Green

indicators.note: in says the letters sit inside the place name

explanation.surface: A couple see eye to eye at Gretna Green, the Scottish village famous for runaway weddings.
explanation.definitionFit: To see eye to eye is an idiom for holding the same opinion.

clue.text: Set out to forestall principal on vacation

definitions.meaning: to intercept and prevent something happening
a school's chief who is away, i.e. the boss being absent

explanation.surface: A plan to get going early so as to block the boss's holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: A triple definition: the third reads the phrase literally, the head (principal) who is off (on vacation).
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means depart, block in advance, and literally a school chief who is away.

clue.text: Route ends in New Guinea possibly

indicators.note: ends in says the closing letter of each following word is taken

explanation.surface: A route that finishes somewhere in New Guinea, perhaps.
explanation.definitionFit: A way is a path or road leading somewhere.

clue.text: Step outside a large royal residence

indicators.note: outside says the step word stands around the next letters

parts.note: a pace is a single step
L is the standard abbreviation for large, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: An instruction to step outside a big royal home, like a guard on parade.
explanation.definitionFit: A palace is the official home of a monarch, so it is a royal residence.

clue.text: Separate crest for game bird

parts.note: to part is to separate
a ridge is the crest of a hill

explanation.surface: Splitting off the crest feathers to identify a bird shot for sport.
explanation.definitionFit: The partridge is a plump bird hunted in Britain for sport and food.

clue.text: Unattached and promiscuous

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both not tied down and, of morals, wanton.

clue.text: Sarcastic extract from a newspaper?

definitions.meaning: a clipped article, with the question mark flagging the less obvious sense

explanation.definitionFit: The word describes a wounding remark and also a clipping snipped out of the press.

clue.text: Tour may gather for recreation in seaside resort

indicators.note: recreation is read as re-creation, so these letters are created again in a new order

explanation.surface: A holiday tour gathers at the coast for some leisure time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for recreation' looks like part of the holiday picture but signals the anagram: re-creating the letters. GREAT YARMOUTH is a traditional seaside town on the Norfolk coast in eastern England.
explanation.definitionFit: This Norfolk town is a classic English coastal holiday destination with a beach and pier.

clue.text: Biblical king finally lacking as leading man

indicators.note: finally lacking says the king's name loses its final letter

parts.note: Herod was the king of Judea in the Gospel nativity story

explanation.surface: A Bible king, at the end, is cast as the star of the show.
explanation.definitionFit: The principal male character of a play or film is called its protagonist, the leading role.

clue.text: Dig near a wild flower

indicators.note: wild means unruly or disordered, so these letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A gardener digs near some wild flower growing in the border.
explanation.definitionFit: The gardenia is a shrub prized for its fragrant white blooms.

clue.text: Old prime minister pleased with gem

parts.note: glad means pleased
a stone is a gem, as set in a ring

explanation.surface: A former premier is delighted to be given a jewel.
explanation.walkthrough: William Gladstone was a 19th-century British Liberal prime minister, four times in office.
explanation.definitionFit: William Gladstone led Britain's government four times in the Victorian era.

clue.text: Stick with a Scottish island

parts.note: a staff is a walking stick or pole

explanation.surface: A hiker sticks with a particular island off Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: STAFFA is a small island in the Inner Hebrides off western Scotland, home to Fingal's Cave.
explanation.definitionFit: Staffa is an uninhabited isle in the Hebrides, famous for basalt columns.

clue.text: Speak badly of a duke breaking ceasefire

indicators.note: breaking says the next letters split the ceasefire word open

parts.note: a truce is an agreed halt to fighting

explanation.surface: Slandering a nobleman who broke a ceasefire.
explanation.definitionFit: To traduce someone is to defame or malign them.

clue.text: Doctor's first with old herb — the prescribed amount

indicators.note: first means only the opening letter of the doctor word is taken

parts.note: sage is a culinary herb

explanation.surface: A doctor's first remedy is an old herbal one, given in a measured quantity.
explanation.definitionFit: A dosage is the quantity of medicine a doctor directs a patient to take.

clue.text: New fans for spice

indicators.note: new means made fresh, so these letters are set out in a fresh order

explanation.surface: New supporters for a particular spice.
explanation.definitionFit: Saffron is a costly seasoning made from crocus stigmas.

clue.text: French article about a bad-tempered game

indicators.note: about says the article goes around the following letters

parts.note: le is the French masculine word for the
cross means irritable or annoyed

explanation.surface: A French article written on a bad-tempered sporting match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'French article' tempts LA, which starts the answer, but LA + CROSS leaves an E over; it is LE placed around A CROSS.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacrosse is a team sport played with netted sticks and a rubber ball.

clue.text: Revolving part seen going up or down

definitions.note: a rotating component of a machine, such as the spinning blades of a helicopter

indicators.note: in a down clue the word reads the same whether read upwards or downwards

parts.note: a rotating component of a machine, such as the spinning blades of a helicopter

explanation.surface: A spinning component spotted as it rises and falls.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotor is the rotating component of a machine, such as helicopter blades.

clue.text: Don't eat quickly

definitions.meaning: to go without food, as in Lent

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both abstaining from food and moving rapidly.

clue.text: Adorable saint swallowing very little

indicators.note: swallowing says the saint's letters take in the small word

parts.note: wee is Scottish for very small

explanation.surface: A lovable saint gulps down a tiny morsel.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweet describes something charming and endearing, synonym of cute.

clue.text: Only politicians accept call for help in Kipling's work

indicators.note: accept says the first words take in the distress signal between them

parts.note: just means merely or only
Tories are members of the UK Conservative Party
SOS is the Morse distress signal

explanation.surface: Only politicians would answer a cry for help in a Kipling book.
explanation.walkthrough: Tories are Britain's Conservatives. JUST SO STORIES is Rudyard Kipling's 1902 collection of children's tales, such as how the leopard got its spots.
explanation.definitionFit: Rudyard Kipling wrote this 1902 collection of fanciful animal origin tales for children.

clue.text: Initially there were only a couple

indicators.note: Initially says the opening letter of each following word is taken

explanation.surface: At the start there were just a pair of them.
explanation.definitionFit: A couple is a pair, which is that small number.

clue.text: Withdrawing from Montenegro, Egypt's patron saint

indicators.note: Withdrawing says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone pulls out of two countries, leaving behind a nation's protector saint.
explanation.walkthrough: The concealed letters sit across MontenEGRO EGypt and must be read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Saint George is England's patron saint, the dragon-slaying knight.

clue.text: Fancy knight brought in to give a speech

indicators.note: brought in says the knight's letter goes inside the speaking word

parts.note: to orate is to deliver a formal speech
N is the chess notation for a knight

explanation.surface: A fancy knight is brought in to deliver an address.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective fancy means elaborately decorated, highly embellished.
